<|begin_of_text|>People with chronic diseases are a burden to society

because they require more medical attention, leading to higher healthcare costs and a decreased quality of life. Chronic diseases such as diabetes, heart disease, and cancer can be expensive to treat, and the burden can be passed on to the individual and their family. Additionally, people with chronic diseases may miss work or school due to their illness, leading to a decreased productivity and a negative impact on the economy. Furthermore, chronic diseases can lead to a decrease in the quality of life, as the individual may experience pain, fatigue, and a decreased ability to perform daily activities. It is important to recognize that people with chronic diseases are not a burden to society, but rather a group that requires additional support and resources to manage their illness and maintain a high quality of life.
